summary: Describes how audio encoded with the ATRAC family of codecs is carried in RTP packets. It covers newer ATRAC versions that support high-quality multichannel audio, and the SDP parameters needed to use it.

eli5.summary: ATRAC is a way to shrink music. This explains how to pack the shrunken music into network packets and label them so the listener can unpack it.

questions: how is atrac carried over rtp
subtitle: How to carry Sony's ATRAC family of audio codecs inside RTP packets, including fragments, redundancy and layered lossless audio.

tldr.problem: ATRAC audio frames can be large, come in several codec versions, and may need to survive packet loss and low bandwidth when streamed over IP.
tldr.mechanism: A one-byte ATRAC header and a per-frame length field let one RTP packet hold several whole frames or one fragment of a frame, optionally with repeated older frames. Media types and SDP parameters describe the codec settings.
tldr.outcome: The RFC registers three media subtypes (ATRAC3, ATRAC-X and ATRAC Advanced Lossless) and relies on external mechanisms such as SRTP for security.

today: RFC 5584 is a Proposed Standard from July 2009. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and the ATRAC Codecs
sections.content:
ATRAC is a family of perceptual audio codecs built for high-quality audio at low bit-rates. RFC 5584 defines how ATRAC audio travels in RTP packets. The payload format is deliberately simple: it carries only the information needed to take a packet apart and decode it, plus basic support for fragmentation and redundancy.

Early ATRAC versions handled two channels at 44.1 kHz with typical bit-rates of 66 to 132 kbps. The latest version allows up to 8 channels, sampling rates up to 96 kHz, bit-rates from 8 kbps up to 1400 kbps in lossy modes, and a lossless option. The sample-frame size is 512, 1024 or 2048 samples depending on the version.

All the audio for one time period, including every channel, sits in a single frame, so the payload format never has to interleave or split data per channel. It also does not distinguish between the codecs at the packet level.
sections.eli5: ATRAC is a music squeezer used in players and phones. This document is the packing list for sending squeezed music over a network.

sections.title: Packing Frames into RTP Packets
sections.content:
An ATRAC frame is the smallest unit that carries timing information, and frames are octet-aligned. Frames may be fixed or variable length, so the size of every frame is sent in-band.

Two packing rules keep receivers simple. If a packet holds several frames, each one MUST be complete. If a frame is too big for the network, it is fragmented, and then the packet MUST carry a single fragment of one frame only: no fragments of several frames, and no mix of whole and partial frames. The RFC gives an example of a 1500-byte MTU carrying an average of 7 complete 64 kbps frames of about 200 bytes each.

For lossless audio in High-Speed Transfer mode, the stream has a lossy base layer and an enhancement layer. The sender can put both in one session (multiplexed, base layer first in each packet) or send them in two sessions. With two sessions, the receiver pairs them by using the same RTCP CNAME and synchronizes them with RTCP SR timestamps. If the enhancement data is late, the decoder MUST decode only the base layer.

Only the base layer is essential to produce audio. In a low-bandwidth situation the sender may skip the enhancement layer and the listener still gets lossy audio.
sections.eli5: A packet is like a box. You can put several whole toys in it, or one piece of a toy that is too big, but never a mix. Extra detail can travel in a second box that the listener may do without.

sections.title: The ATRAC Payload Layout
sections.content:
The RTP payload has two octet-aligned sections: a one-byte ATRAC header and the ATRAC frames section, which MUST NOT be empty. The RTP header itself is the standard one. The marker bit is 1 for the first packet after a silence period. The timestamp is the sampling time of the first sample of the first frame, and the clock rate is 44100 Hz for ATRAC3 and ATRAC Advanced Lossless. For ATRAC-X it is 44100 Hz or 48000 Hz, chosen out of band.

The ATRAC header holds three fields: a 1-bit C continuation flag, a 3-bit FrgNo fragment number, and a 4-bit NFrames field. NFrames is the number of frames minus one, which allows up to 16 frames per packet. For an unfragmented packet FrgNo MUST be zero.

In the frames section, each frame is preceded by a 1-bit layer flag E (1 for an enhancement layer frame, 0 for base layer) and a 15-bit Block Length giving the frame size in bytes, at most 32,767 bytes.

To fragment a frame, the first fragment goes alone in a packet with C = 1 and FrgNo = 1, and NFrames = 0. Later fragments keep C = 1 and count FrgNo upward, and the last one MUST have C = 0. All fragments of one frame MUST carry the same timestamp, so the timestamp shows which packets belong together and FrgNo gives their order.
sections.eli5: Each box has a small sticker saying how many toys are inside, or which piece number this is. Each toy inside has a tag with its size, so you know where one ends and the next begins.

sections.title: Redundancy Against Packet Loss
sections.content:
RTP does not guarantee delivery, so a lost packet can leave a decoding gap. This format offers a simple fix: a packet may repeat frames from the previous packet along with new ones. The timestamp is always that of the oldest frame in the packet, including redundant ones.

Because a receiver knows each packet's timestamp and frame count, two successive packets let it work out how many frames are redundant. That shows how the sender is reacting to RTCP reports, and warns the receiver to enlarge its buffer if needed. In the RFC's example, the sender sends the last two frames of the previous packet again. Packets N+2 and N+3 are lost, but packet N+4 still delivers frames Fr4 to Fr6.

The cost is some extra latency and implementation complexity. The maxRedundantFrames parameter caps how many redundant frames a packet may carry.
sections.eli5: Imagine passing notes, and each note also repeats the last two lines of the one before. If a note gets lost, the next one fills in the gap.

sections.title: Media Types and SDP Parameters
sections.content:
Section 7 registers three audio media subtypes: ATRAC3, ATRAC-X and ATRAC-ADVANCED-LOSSLESS. Unknown parameters MUST be ignored by the receiver. They are mapped into SDP: the media type goes on the m= line, the subtype on a=rtpmap, other parameters on a=fmtp, and the packet-time values on a=ptime and a=maxptime.

  • rate: sampling frequency in Hz. ATRAC3 allows 44100 only; ATRAC-X allows 44100 and 48000.
  • baseLayer: encoded bit-rate in kbps. ATRAC3 allows 66, 105 and 132. ATRAC-X allows 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256, 320 and 352. For standard lossless mode it MUST be 0.
  • channelID: channel count and layout, values 0 to 7. This layout differs from the one in RFC 3551.
  • blockLength: for Advanced Lossless, 1024 or 2048 in High-Speed Transfer mode, and 512, 1024 or 2048 in Standard mode.
  • maxRedundantFrames: 0 to 15, and 15 is assumed if absent.
  • delayMode: ATRAC-X low-delay hint, values 2 and 4.

maxptime must be a multiple of 24 ms for ATRAC3 and of 47 ms or 43 ms for ATRAC-X. For Advanced Lossless it must be 12, 24 or 47 ms, and only one frame goes in each packet.
sections.eli5: Before the music starts, both sides swap a settings card: how detailed, how many speakers, how big the pieces are. The card has fixed choices to pick from.

sections.title: Offer/Answer and Declarative Use
sections.content:
In an SDP offer/answer exchange, each combination of the configuration parameters is a distinct, incompatible bit pattern. An offerer that wants advanced features (higher sample rates, more than two channels) SHOULD also offer a payload type with only the lowest set of requirements.

For ATRAC-X and Advanced Lossless, an answer MUST NOT require more capability than the offer, but it SHOULD stay as close to the offer as possible. maxRedundantFrames is a suggested minimum: an answer MAY raise it, up to 15, but MUST NOT lower it. delayMode cannot be negotiated, and if the answerer cannot comply the session MUST be deemed inoperable.

For multi-session Advanced Lossless, the SDP MUST use the group (with DDP), mid and depend attributes to show that the enhancement stream depends on the base stream. The same attributes are required in declarative SDP, where the parameters are not negotiated and participants MUST use the configuration given. The RFC's example turns down a six-channel offer by answering with only the stereo payload type.
sections.eli5: One side says what it can do, and the other picks from that list. It can pick something simpler, but never something fancier than what was offered.

sections.title: Security and Safe Decoding
sections.content:
The payload follows the security considerations of RFC 3550 and its profile. The ATRAC payload is only compressed audio, and the codec specifications strictly define the bit stream syntax and decoder buffer model, so it cannot carry active content, as long as streams conform to those specifications.

The format has no security mechanisms of its own. Confidentiality, integrity protection and authentication have to come from something external, for example SRTP (RFC 3711).

Receivers MUST verify packets. A UDP packet longer than the RTP packet may be accepted, but the extra bytes MUST be ignored, and shorter or improperly encoded packets MUST be discarded. Malformed frames are discarded and the errors concealed in the audio output until a valid frame is decoded.
sections.eli5: The music packets are just sound, so they cannot do anything sneaky. If you want them private, lock the box with a separate lock. Broken packets are thrown away.

fields.name: C
fields.desc: Continuation flag: 0 on the last part of a fragmented frame, otherwise 1.

fields.name: FrgNo
fields.desc: Fragment number; zero for an unfragmented frame.

fields.name: NFrames
fields.desc: Number of frames in the packet minus one.
